definition: Threat appraisal is a person’s assessment of how threatening a situation or event feels to them. In the source context, higher threat appraisal means feeling more threatened by a heart attack and is linked with greater rumination and higher depression scores.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit definition of “threat appraisal” as a person’s assessment of how threatening a situation feels to them; it only discusses it as a cognitive factor measured in post-myocardial-infarction patients.
The definition’s general phrasing (“how threatening a situation or event feels”) is not directly supported by the packet text provided.

While the packet supports that higher threat appraisal is hypothesized to relate to rumination and higher depression scores after a myocardial infarction, the packet does not clearly support the specific wording that higher threat appraisal means “feeling more threatened by a heart attack” (it mentions the MI context but does not define the subjective ‘feeling’ aspect).
The added context about rumination and higher depression scores is drawn from hypotheses in the source article, not established findings, so it should not be presented as a confirmed relationship.
The definition generalizes a study-specific post-myocardial-infarction use of the term into a broad generic definition without support from the packet.
The source supports threat appraisal in a cardiac context, but not the broader claim that it is simply a person’s assessment of how threatening any situation or event feels.
